title: Safety-Certified EEGNet via Semidefinite Programming for Implantable BCIs
summary: We present a safety-certified EEGNet variant using semidefinite programming (SDP) to provide formal robustness guarantees for implantable BCIs. By bounding output variations under input perturbations, the model ensures reliable operation in safety-critical scenarios. Validation includes SDP-based verification and physical adversarial testing on motor imagery datasets.
gap: Implantable BCIs require provable safety guarantees, but existing EEG models lack formal robustness certification. SDP methods from [ref-005] and [ref-020] are untested in EEG domains, leaving a gap in certified robust BCI design.
approach: Apply SDP-based quadratic constraint programming to EEGNet, modeling activation functions as convex potentials. Derive layer-wise Lipschitz bounds via SDP relaxation, ensuring output stability under bounded input perturbations during inference.
evaluation: Compare certified robustness bounds with empirical attack success rates on motor imagery datasets. Metrics include verified perturbation radii, CLEVER scores, and comparison with Parseval EEGNet. Physical adversarial testing uses noise-injected EEG signals from [ref-006].
